subject: SKUOnboarding launch — temporary quota/throughput exception request
messages:
From: Elena Soto <elena@skuonboarding.com>
To: stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai
Cc: ops@skuonboarding.com
Date: 2026-09-07T14:12:00-07:00
Subject: SKUOnboarding pre-launch traffic spike — quota uplift request

Hi Stephanie,

We're ramping SKUOnboarding's public launch the week of Sep 21. Our internal load tests show a burst profile of ~1.8M tokens/min (peak) for the first 48 hours, then settling to ~300k tokens/min. We need a temporary quota increase and a higher per-route RPS to avoid 429s during day-one signups.

Ask:
- Temporary per-tenant token quota: 150M tokens/day (for 72 hours starting 2026-09-21T00:00Z)
- Per-route RPS: allow up to 600 RPS on inference endpoint /v1/generate

Attached: SKUOnboarding_traffic_forecast_Q4.csv (detailed hourly forecast), and we can share a signed MOU for exceptions.

Can Redwood confirm if this is feasible and what guardrails you recommend (fallback model, throttling windows)? If you prefer a call, we're available tomorrow morning PT.

Thanks,

Elena Soto
Head of Infrastructure
SKUOnboarding
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>
To: vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai, rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-09-07T16:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SKUOnboarding pre-launch traffic spike — quota uplift request

Vivek / Rishi — looping you in. Elena just sent their Q4 forecast and is asking for a temporary uplift for the Sep 21 launch. Key asks: 150M tokens/day for 72 hours and 600 RPS on the generate route.

Questions/asks from product/ops side:
- Can we support a 600 RPS per-route cap for a single tenant without impacting multi-tenant latency SLOs?
- If we prefer a graduated ramp, what numbers would you require for a canary?
- Any recommended fallback model variants or reduced-quality quantized models to use as a safety net?

I've attached their forecast file to the thread. If we can get a short runbook (steps + rollback criteria) and an estimate of infra risk, I will reply with Redwood's proposal and timeline.

I'd like to avoid a long legal redline loop — if we agree operationally, I'll share our temp_quota_agreement.docx to speed signatures.

— Steph
Stephanie Nguyen
Director, Sales Engineering
Redwood Inference
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai, rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-09-08T09:25:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SKUOnboarding pre-launch traffic spike — quota uplift request

On Tue, Sep 7, 2026 at 4:03 PM PDT Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Vivek / Rishi — looping you in. Elena just sent their Q4 forecast and is asking for a temporary uplift for the Sep 21 launch.

Thanks for the context. Quick operational thoughts:

- Feasibility: We can accommodate a temporary per-tenant spike of this size but not at full model capacity. Recommendation is to grant a time-limited quota exception tied to two constraints: (1) a staged ramp (canary → 50% → 100%) and (2) mandatory fallback to the quantized v2-small variant if system-wide GPU occupancy exceeds 85%.

- Suggested plan (72-hour window):
  * Hour 0–4 (canary): 100 RPS directed to a warm pool (single shard) to validate correctness and KV cache warmup.
  * Hour 5–18: 300 RPS (spread across 3 shards) — monitor lat p99 and GPU queue length.
  * Hour 19–72: ramp to 600 RPS if p99 < 350ms and GPU occupancy < 80% for two consecutive 5-min windows.

- Token quota: approve 150M tokens/day for the 72-hour window conditional on the above ramp behavior and exec confirmation from sales/legal for the temporary MOU.

- Guardrails: automated rollback trigger if (a) system-wide p99 > 800ms for 10m, (b) sustained GPU occupancy > 90% for 5m, or (c) error rate > 2%.

I'll prepare a short runbook and will need the forecast's hourly rows flattened into a simple RPS curve (attachment looks hourly already). Also need customer to sign temp_quota_agreement.docx before Hour 0.

- Infrastructure constraints: we can provision an extra warm pool (1–2 GPUs) in us-west-2 for the window; cost will be charged as overage on their invoice unless we agree to credits.

— Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
VP, Infrastructure & Reliability
Redwood Inference
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai, vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-09-09T11:07:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SKUOnboarding pre-launch traffic spike — quota uplift request

On Wed, Sep 8, 2026 at 9:25 AM PDT Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai> wrote:
> I'll prepare a short runbook and will need the forecast's hourly rows flattened into a simple RPS curve.

Adding infra specifics and operational caveats:

- Model warmup: Generating cold-start tokens to warm KV cache will cause transient resource pressure. The first 30 minutes of any ramp may see elevated latency; that's why the canary window is important.

- GPU shard sizing: For the requested 600 RPS using standard v2 model at our current perf profile, we estimate needing ~3.5 dedicated v100-equivalent GPUs if fully allocated. To avoid denying other customers, we propose using an isolated warm pool of 2 GPUs + burst to shared pool and enforce the quantized fallback at 80% occupancy.

- Safety automation: I will add two autoscaling hooks for this event: (1) time-bound burst scaling (max +2 GPUs) and (2) preemptive throttling controller that enforces the staged ramp rules automatically. Both will be toggled for the event window.

- Rollback & comms: If we trigger rollback, we will send automated notices to ops@skuonboarding.com and to a single Redwood on-call alias. Please confirm the external contact list and two emergency Slack numbers.

I'll attach a brief ops checklist in the runbook. Once Steph confirms we can present to the customer, I will schedule the extra pool provisioning.

— Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Sr. Manager, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Soto <elena@skuonboarding.com>

Date: 2026-09-10T10:45:00-07:00
Subject: RE: SKUOnboarding pre-launch traffic spike — quota uplift request

Elena — thanks for the forecast and for being responsive. We've reviewed internally and can support a temporary exception with the following conditions:

Proposal (summary):
- Approved temporary token quota: 150M tokens/day for 72 hours starting 2026-09-21T00:00Z.
- Approved per-route throughput: staged ramp to a maximum of 600 RPS (see staged schedule below).
- Guardrails: automated rollback triggers (p99, GPU occupancy, error rate) and mandatory fallback to quantized v2-small when occupancy hits 80%.
- Infra: Redwood will provision an isolated warm pool (2 GPUs) and allow burst +2 GPUs to shared pool as needed. Extra capacity will be invoiced as overage unless we agree to a credit.

Staged ramp (approved):
- Hour 0–4: 100 RPS (canary)
- Hour 5–18: 300 RPS
- Hour 19–72: 600 RPS if health checks pass

Next steps (for you):
1) Sign and return temp_quota_agreement.docx (attached) — required to finalize provisioning.
2) Confirm two Slack contacts and the ops email (we will send rollback notices there).
3) Confirm whether you want Redwood to enable the quantized v2-small fallback automatically or only after manual approval.

I've attached our mutual_action_plan_SKUOnboarding.pdf and the proposed agreement. Vivek and Rishi have prepared the runbook and scaling hooks; they will provision the warm pool once we receive the signed agreement.

If a short call would help, I can set 30 minutes tomorrow morning PT to walk through the runbook and finalize signatures.

Best,

— Steph
Stephanie Nguyen
Director, Sales Engineering
Redwood Inference
